newsitem.title: UK: Arabica coffee prices to fall in 1998--EIU.
newsitem.headline: Arabica coffee prices to fall in 1998--EIU.

text.p: Arabica coffee prices could fall by a sharp 22.3 percent to 148.80 U.S. cents a lb in 1998 from 191.3 cents this year, the Economist Intelligence Unit said on Monday.
Prices for the less valued robusta beans could average 76.10 cents in 1998, down by 9.3 percent from 83.90 this year.

But cocoa could buck the trend, rising by 12.0 percent to 80.5 cents a lb in 1998 year-on-year, the London think-tank said in its latest issue of world commodity forecasts: food, feedstuffs and beverages (FFB).
Other major gainers in 1998 would include sorghum and maize, each rising by 12.3 and 12 percent to 130 and 135 cents respectively.
Palm oil, soybean meal and sunflower oil -- falling by between 6.6 and 16.8 percent -- rank high on the 1998 losers' list which is led by arabica coffee, the EIU said.
It said the EIU's soft commodity index (FFB) would fall by 5.5 percent overall in 1997 owning to a sharp decline in grain and sugar prices.

The decline will slow in 1998 and 1999 as the anticipated sharp downward correction in coffee prices, coupled with falling edible oil prices, more than offset tightening fundamentals in the grain and sugar markets.
On coffee, Karen St Jean, an EIU commodities analyst and editor of the report, said:
"Further increases in shop prices cannot be avoided in the short term, especially as retailers have run down stocks built up earlier in 1997 before the boom started."
"However, assuming there is no crop disaster in Brazil, wholesale prices will fall sharply before the end of the year," she added in a statement. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
